faults.failure: CHK-001 (assertion) 'pcpi_wait stays asserted until pcpi_ready' — 2809 fails / 278073 hits, first fail at 480000 ps (sim.log:39). Fails also occur in groups exactly 370000 ps apart (sim.log:49-51: 19035000, 19405000, 19775000).
faults.spec_says: spec/c_pcpi_div_Design_Specification.md:62-66 (rule PD-T1.1-06, SHOULD, rules.json:164-186): "A PCPI core that needs more than a couple of cycles to execute an instruction, should assert `pcpi_wait` as soon as the instruction has been decoded successfully and keep it asserted until it asserts `pcpi_ready`." Master side (PD-T1.1-01, spec :48-52) only says pcpi_valid is asserted with the instruction. The spec never says whether the master must drop pcpi_valid between two instructions. contract.json:327 (assumption) says: "Legal master stimulus holds pcpi_valid ... stable from issue until pcpi_ready=1 is sampled, and deasserts pcpi_valid on the following cycle." contract.json:223 (CHK-008 stimulus) says: "then drive pcpi_valid=0 on the next cycle". So the real core always gives at least one edge with pcpi_valid=0 between PCPI instructions. rules.json:720-721 records the open question on PD-T1.1-06 timing ('more than a couple of cycles', 'as soon as').
faults.verification_does: verif/tests/test_c_pcpi_div.py:214-217: after the ready edge, execute() does `await next_cycle; self.drive(0); self.sample(chk)` and returns without waiting for another cycle. idle(gap) (160-167) does `next_cycle` then drive for each of gap iterations, so with gap=0 it does nothing. The next execute() then calls `self.drive(1, insn, rs1, rs2)` at line 181 in the same mid-cycle, which overwrites the pcpi_valid=0 just written. gap=0 is common: CHK-004 randint(0,2) (273), CHK-005 randint(0,3) (295), CHK-008 gap in (0,1,5) (329), regression 50% gap=0 (395-396). The Python model still records self.valid=0 for that cycle (131), so its own CHK-003 check (154-157) and its wait check (186-206) do not see a problem. The wait sampled at the issue edge (182) is never checked, and first_wait is only tracked from j=1. Evidence that the deassert edge is missing: latency is 36 edges (sim.log:35). With a real valid=0 edge, back-to-back instructions repeat every 38 edges (380 ns at the 10 ns clock implied by 26 cases × ~38 edges ≈ 9975 ns). The log shows failures exactly 370000 ps (37 edges) apart (sim.log:49-51, 70-74, 104-107). In results.json:201,225, COVP-029 'Back-to-back division requests' (nnc_cov.sv:143-144: valid && is_div && !prev_out && prev_ready_q, so valid high right after a ready edge) = 2809. COVP-005 'Wait high in first cycle of a division request' = 2809. Both equal the CHK-001 fail count exactly. The first fail at 480 ns falls inside test_chk_004 (0–9975 ns); its sim.log line comes after the test-start banner only because of output ordering.
faults.what_to_change: Fix test: make sure at least one rising edge samples pcpi_valid=0 between instructions, as contract.json:223/327 require. Alternatively, have idle() always run at least one cycle. Expected result: CHK-001 fails drop to 0, and back-to-back spacing becomes 38 edges. This changes upstream code. Clarify spec: add a stated master rule (e.g. Then align contract.json:327 and the test with it. The check itself should stay as it is.

changes.why: execute() drove pcpi_valid=1 in the same mid-cycle where the previous deassert (or the last idle cycle) had just driven pcpi_valid=0. That overwrote the 0, so with gap=0 no rising edge ever saw pcpi_valid=0 between two instructions. The test's own model still recorded valid=0, so it missed this. The contract says the master deasserts pcpi_valid on the cycle after pcpi_ready, so this stimulus was illegal and set off the CHK-001 failures. The fix waits one clock cycle (await next_cycle) at the start of execute() before driving the issue. Now the pcpi_valid=0 that was already driven and checked is really sampled at a rising edge, so every instruction is preceded by at least one pcpi_valid=0 edge. CHK-001 in the SVA, the cover points and all expected values are unchanged.
spec_refs: contract.json:223 (CHK-008 stimulus: 'then drive pcpi_valid=0 on the next cycle')
